Iconicity ratings for signs of German Sign Language

Source: R/data.R
dgs_iconicity.Rd

30 deaf signers of German Sign Language (DGS) and 30 hearing non-signers rate 300 DGS signs for iconicity (1 = not iconic, 7 = very iconic). Ratings by the two groups are correlated (r about 0.78 for sign means, as in Trettenbrein et al. 2021). Signers rate signs as more iconic overall, and non-signers rate verbs as more iconic than nouns. More iconic signs are acquired earlier. For mixed models of ratings with crossed raters and items.

Usage

dgs_iconicity

Format

A tibble with 18000 rows and 7 columns:

rater

Rater ID, R01 to R60.

group

"hearing non-signer" or "deaf signer".

sign

Sign ID, sign001 to sign300.

category

"noun" or "verb".

handedness

"one-handed" or "two-handed"; no effect.

aoa

Age of acquisition of the sign in years, as rated by deaf signers.

rating

Iconicity rating, 1 to 7.

Source

data-raw/dgs_iconicity.R

Details

True model:

rating = 3.3 + iconicity + g0 + r0 + signer + 0.5 * verb * non_signer + e

rounded and limited to 1-7. Each sign's iconicity has SD 1.2, g0 is a deviation of each sign within each group (SD 0.6), raters differ by SD 0.5 and e has SD 0.9. Age of acquisition is 5.5 - 0.6 * iconicity years plus noise (SD 1.3). The group differences follow findings for DGS (signers higher) and for ASL (Sehyr and Emmorey 2019) and Israeli Sign Language (Fuks 2023) (verbs higher for non-signers).

References

Trettenbrein, P. C., Pendzich, N.-K., Cramer, J.-M., Steinbach, M. & Zaccarella, E. (2021). Psycholinguistic norms for more than 300 lexical signs in German Sign Language (DGS). Behavior Research Methods, 53(5), 1817-1832. doi:10.3758/s13428-020-01524-y

Fuks, O. (2023). Iconicity perception under the lens of iconicity rating and transparency tasks in Israeli Sign Language (ISL). Sign Language Studies, 24(1), 46-92.

Sehyr, Z. S. & Emmorey, K. (2019). The perceived mapping between form and meaning in American Sign Language depends on linguistic knowledge and task: Evidence from iconicity and transparency judgments. Language and Cognition, 11(2), 208-234. doi:10.1017/langcog.2019.18

Thompson, R. L., Vinson, D. P., Woll, B. & Vigliocco, G. (2012). The road to language learning is iconic: Evidence from British Sign Language. Psychological Science, 23(12), 1443-1448. doi:10.1177/0956797612459763

Examples

round(tapply(dgs_iconicity$rating, dgs_iconicity[c("group", "category")], mean), 2)
#>                     category
#> group                noun verb
#>   hearing non-signer 3.51 3.95
#>   deaf signer        4.37 4.47
signs <- aggregate(rating ~ sign + group, data = dgs_iconicity, FUN = mean)
signs <- reshape(signs, idvar = "sign", timevar = "group", direction = "wide")
cor(signs[, 2], signs[, 3])
#> [1] 0.7814731
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::lmer(rating ~ group * category + (1 | rater) + (1 | sign), data = dgs_iconicity)
  lme4::fixef(m)
}
#>                   (Intercept)              groupdeaf signer 
#>                     3.5124260                     0.8609467 
#>                  categoryverb groupdeaf signer:categoryverb 
#>                     0.4425358                    -0.3428806
